title: Wake, Agni, and keep watch over him

words.meaning: sacrifice and pious works (what is offered and what is given)
words.context: Sāyaṇa: «श्रौतस्मार्तकर्मणी», the rites of the Veda and of smṛti

words.meaning: may you two join, bring together
words.role: verb of the second clause, its subject ‘you and he’
with ca: ‘and he’ — the sacrificer, joined to Agni as a subject
joins ayam to the ‘you’ of the verb

words.meaning: has stretched along; may he stretch
words.role: main verb of the second line

words.context: Sāyaṇa: the stream of the sacrifice, «यज्ञप्रवाहम्»

sandhi.rule: i before a vowel becomes y
a final n before t is written ṃs (P. 8.3.7 (नश्छव्यप्रशान्))

samasa.meaning: what is sacrificed and what is given (wells, gifts, works for others)

morphology.note: s-aorist of √tan with the preverbs anu and ā; the Saṃhitā spells the nasal as anusvāra before s.

translation.literal: Wake up, Agni; watch over him; may you two join sacrifice and gift, [you] and this one. Again making you a father, a young one, he has stretched along this thread in you.
translation.readable: Wake, Agni, and keep watch over him; together with him bring about what is offered and what is given. Making you young and a father again, he has drawn this thread of the rite through you.

meaning: A verse of the fire-altar books of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (4.7.13). Agni is told to wake and watch over the sacrificer, and the two of them, Agni and he, are to bring about together the rites and the good works — iṣṭāpūrta, what is offered in sacrifice and what is given for the good of others. The second half speaks of the sacrificer, or of Agni, renewing the fire, making him a young father again, and stretching the thread of the rite through him. Sāyaṇa reads iṣṭāpūrta as the rites of the Veda and of smṛti, and the thread as the unbroken course of the sacrifice. The verse addresses Agni; the verb it opens with, budh, ‘wake’, is the root of the graha’s name, Budha, ‘the wakeful’.
in_the_rite: The mantra of Budha (Mercury), first of the three in his step of the Navagraha sūktam (witness S). The verse itself addresses Agni; the word that links it to Budha is its first, ud-budhyasva, from the same root. Its use for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa on TS 4.7.13: Agni is to rouse himself and keep the sacrificer alert; then «अयं च त्वं च मिलित्वेष्टापूर्ते श्रौतस्मार्तकर्मणी संसृजेथां संपादयतम्» — ‘he and you together, bring about iṣṭa and pūrta, the rites of śruti and smṛti’; and Agni, making the sacrificer young again, «एतं तन्तुं यज्ञप्रवाहमन्वातांसीदनुक्रमेण तनोतु» — ‘may he stretch out this thread, the stream of the sacrifice, in due order’.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: A triṣṭubh (eleven syllables to the pāda); the Saṃhitā prints its two halves as two lines.
